paraphrase: Whatever can fail to be r (in the two-way sense of the potency of the contradictory, able to be r and able not to be r) can be otherwise in respect r. Read from In Metaph. V, lect. 6 n. 14 (what can be in more ways can be otherwise and otherwise; claim AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-V-L6-MORE-WAYS-OTHERWISE-A), counting the two-way potency as being able to be in two ways in r and taking r as the respect of being otherwise. Aristotle, Met. V.5 does not state it (1015b11-15 argues the converse).
